summary: High-volume fanout deadlock causing streaming stalls for Starlight Warehouse - escalation and post-incident follow-up
description: Issue summary: Between 2026-03-01 02:14 UTC and 2026-03-01 03:05 UTC Starlight Warehouse experienced widespread streaming stalls and 5xx errors for batched inference jobs. Impact: Customer reported stalled streaming responses, duplicate retry amplification when client retried, and delayed order confirmations in their downstream systems. Immediate effect: customer-facing SLA exposure and an urgent escalation to Redwood Support and SRE. This ticket tracks the incident, engineering investigation, mitigation, and post-incident follow-up including billing reconciliation.
impact: ~27 minutes of full fanout deadlock for high-concurrency batch job class; ~14k affected requests; transient duplicate completions observed when client retried; estimated billing exposure ~ $1.2k in overage credits to be issued.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Submit a 10k-batch request across 200 simultaneous sessions to model revgen-2.1 with streaming enabled and prefix caching turned on
2) Observe request fanout to edge multiplexer and scheduler while targets shift between dedicated and shared pools
3) Under sustained high-concurrency, monitor scheduler queue growth and stream connector backpressure until connectors hit deadlock and stall streams
4) Retry the original client requests immediately to see duplicate completions when partial responses are eventually flushed
comments: 2026-03-01 02:20 - Maya Chen (Support): Customer reported that streaming responses stopped mid-transcript and their orchestration retried aggressively. Opening Sev0 and paging SRE.

2026-03-01 02:25 - Diego Alvarez (SRE): Initial hypothesis: scheduler queue growth + connector threadpool exhaustion causing head-of-line blocking. Collecting heap/kernel metrics and connector traces.

2026-03-01 02:40 - Diego Alvarez (SRE): Observed multiplexer connector deadlocks tied to an edge case in our connector backoff where connector A holds a lock waiting for connector B acknowledgment while B is stuck waiting on a scheduler ticket. Increasing connector threadpool as temporary mitigation.

2026-03-01 02:50 - Customer (Starlight contact - Priya Rao): Starlight confirms partial transcripts flushed after ~20 seconds and some duplicate completions where retry occurred. They require timeline and credit for impacted requests.
2026-03-01 03:05 - Diego Alvarez (SRE): Deployed emergency patch to connector backoff to break circular wait and scaled dedicated pool for Starlight. Streaming resumed across affected sessions.
2026-03-02 10:15 - Support (Maya): Follow-up call scheduled with customer for 2026-03-03 to review timeline, impact, and remediation plan.
2026-03-09 09:00 - Engineering (Diego): Root cause analysis complete; rolling out permanent fix in serving-runtime and scheduler; drafting postmortem for exec review.
investigation_notes: Trace analysis shows circular wait across multiplexer connectors when scheduler tickets experience large variance in assignment latency under heavy fanout
KV cache aging combined with quantized kernel swap caused occasional long-tail processing for specific worker shards, exacerbating scheduler ticket starvation
Connector backoff algorithm had a missing preemption step that allowed two connectors to enter a lock-wait cycle when processing responses for the same request ID across retries
Autoscaler did not trigger scale fast enough due to conservative CPU-based heuristics; lack of request-rate driven signals delayed pool expansion
resolution: Applied an emergency connector backoff preemption patch (serving-runtime PR #412) and manually scaled Starlight's dedicated pool. After stabilization, deployed a scheduler ticket preemption change (scheduler PR #89) and updated autoscaler to consider request-rate signals. Verified streaming resumed and no further deadlocks observed over 72h of monitoring.
root_cause: A race condition in connector backoff combined with scheduler ticket starvation under high-fanout batch workloads; autoscaler heuristics were insufficiently responsive to request-rate surges.
follow_up_actions: 1) Backport connector preemption patch to all active runtimes (planned hotfix window 2026-03-12)
2) Enhance autoscaler to include request-rate and connector-latency signals; rollout in canary 2026-03-18
3) Add a new alert for connector circular-wait patterns and scheduler ticket age > 5s
4) Conduct targeted load-testing for high-fanout batch patterns with revgen-2.1 variants
5) Customer remediation: issue $1,200 credit and provide technical advisory on client-side retry backoff configuration
billing_impact: Preliminary estimate $1,200 in overage credits due to duplicate completions and retried requests. Finance notified and invoice adjustment in progress.
